title: Volume 1 Chapter 1: Nail Chip 1
content: The story takes a slight step back. A few days after my first conversation with Sayori Goto, I found myself at the shopping mall in front of the station. My target, of course, was the model shop located in one corner of the mall. “Phew, thank goodness—” I sighed in relief as I looked at the latest kits displayed outside. Recently, due to reselling demand, it was not uncommon for the latest kits to sell out immediately upon release. Just seeing them safely on the shelves made me feel at ease.

I—Hajime Azuma—had a hobby of making Plastic Models. Ever since elementary school, I had been endlessly creating models by imitating what I saw. Because of that, I had few friends and was completely unaware of popular TV shows or streamers. However, thanks to my solitary crafting activities, I had managed to create models that were good enough to be featured in magazines. Recently, I had even started a service for making models on behalf of others through the internet. This allowed me to earn some pocket money, which in turn was used for more model-making.

With the latest kit in hand, I wandered around the store, my heart racing with excitement. (Now I just need a sponge file, some solvents… and maybe I should buy some nippers too. The cutting ability of my current nippers is a bit questionable.) I loved browsing model shops. No matter where I looked, there were only tools for model-making. Perhaps it was a modeler's nature to end up buying tools that weren't even necessary.

As I walked through the narrow aisles unique to model shops—“Ehh? Is this right? …But it doesn’t look cute. I wonder if bigger numbers are stronger?”—there was a flashy gal who clearly didn’t belong in a model shop. With horns extending from her blonde hair and a tail peeking out from her skirt—there was no doubt. It was my classmate, Sayori Goto.
“Huh?”
“Ah! Azuma-kun!”
I let out a strange sound, and she immediately noticed me. With the characteristic footwork of a gal, she quickly approached, fast and without hesitation.
“Are you shopping too, Azuma-kun?”
“Uh, yeah, um… I’m looking for the kit that just came out today…”
“Oh, it says new release! Are you going to make it?”
“Well, I mean, I’m planning to…”
Help me, Miyabe! I silently called out to my absent friend. Of course, he wouldn’t come.
“Are you going to make a Plastic Model…?” she asked, a completely obvious question. Of course, I was going to make one since I was in a model shop. But wait, do gals even make models?
“Nope, I don’t know anything about models,” she said, giggling.
“Oh, Azuma-kun, you know a lot, right? Teach me! I was hoping to find some tools here.”
“Tools… um, what kind?”
“Something for filing?”
What for?

No, if she’s looking for something in a model shop, it’s definitely for plastic. Calm down, me. Just because I’m socially awkward doesn’t mean I need to overthink this. I just need to answer her questions plainly.
“If you’re filing, you’d generally use a file or… I think sponge files are easy to use, but, um, it depends on the purpose…”
“I want to file it down strongly, like ‘gari gari gari~’! Something that can file down diamonds!”
“Those kinds of tools aren’t in a model shop.”

Her requests were all too vague. I couldn’t help but interject. I mean, aren’t you filing a model? From the way Sayori spoke, it sounded like she wanted to file something large and hard. In that case, a metal rod file would be suitable.
“Well, for now, something like this file should… probably be easy to use… Start with this to file, and then move to larger grits to finish it nicely…”
“Oh, I see! Just like a shiner!”
Shiner? A word I wasn’t familiar with popped up. Before I could ask what she meant, the gal picked up the file I had recommended.
“Alright, I’ll buy this!”
Her decision was quick, without hesitation—was this what a gal was like?
“Alright! This will definitely be perfect!”
“Uh, I don’t know what you’re making, but… I hope it turns out well,” I said, my honest feelings surfacing.
Sayori responded with a beaming smile.
“Yeah! Thanks, Azuma-kun! Alright, I’ll show you my serious side!”
Sayori Goto was fired up. Who was she saying that to?
With that momentum, she completed her purchase and waved goodbye to me (her tail wagging along) as she left the model shop.
In the end, I missed the chance to ask her what she was planning to use the tools for. (But well, it’s fine.) Even though it was just a trivial piece of advice, I felt like I had done a good deed.

I understood very well the joy of creating something that was originally just seen as an anime or game, transforming it into a Plastic Model right in front of me. Sayori Goto might have something she wanted to create too.

Wishing for her success in her crafting, I also completed my purchase. At that moment, it was just a simple encounter with Sayori Goto at the model shop, and a brief conversation—that was all it was. (Could it be—she bought that file for her nails…?)
Time returned to the present. During lunch break at school, just after being unexpectedly asked by Sayori Goto to do her nails.
“Y-You didn’t buy that file to file your nails, did you!?”
“Yeah, that’s right!”
I felt dizzy. That file was for models. There was no way it was meant for filing nails.
“W-Wait, if you use that, you’ll file your nails down to nothing!?”
“No, look, Azuma-kun!”
Sayori Goto suddenly showed me her hand.
With her palm facing me, her nails were clearly visible. On her five fingers were sharp, golden claws that sparkled brilliantly, unlike human nails.
“Even with that file, it doesn’t file down at all! Isn’t that unbelievable!? In the end, the file got flatter instead!”
“…Are you serious?”

What kind of hardness do those claws have? Sayori Goto’s nails were slightly curved like talons, with sharp tips glimmering. If a metal file couldn’t file them down, wouldn’t they be able to tear through human flesh?—I thought something frightening.
“Being a dragon is really inconvenient! Because of these claws, I can’t do my nails at all!”
Didn’t you just say you got banned from the salon?
“Yeah! All the salon tools are useless, and for some reason, the polish peels off right away, making it look terrible! I can’t believe it!”
“What’s polish…?”
“Oh, it’s the kind of paint used for regular nail polish. You know, the stuff that comes in small bottles?”
So that’s what they call it.

It’s not uncommon for terms that are common in one industry to be unheard of in another. Even modelers have many terms like “sokuzumi” or “awase-me-keshi” that are only used among themselves. (—I guess I really need to learn from scratch if I want to do nails?) I steeled myself, surprised to find that I was already feeling motivated to do Sayori Goto’s nails.
“So, I thought I’d just file them myself since I had no other choice. And you were talking about Plastic Models, right?”
“Uh, yeah.”
It seemed she was referring to the time she had approached me to talk.
“I’ve heard that making models and doing nails are similar! So instead of using nail tools, I thought I could use model tools! I’m a genius!”
“And that’s why you went to the model shop?”
“Yeah! I didn’t expect to run into you, though! Do you go there often?”
“It’s convenient…”

“I see. The shop is definitely spacious, and there were a lot of tools! There were also a ton of colors for painting, just like nail polish! I get excited when I see a lot of colors lined up! It’s so funny!”
She was off on a tangent, and it just kept going. Conversations with a gal were like a runaway train, speeding ahead without stopping even when they derailed.
“Uh, so, you tried filing your nails yourself?”
I tried to steer the conversation back on track as best as I could.
“Yeah! But it didn’t file down at all! Pien!”
She said “pien,” but her expression was all “aha☆.” She didn’t show any negative feelings at all.
“Hey, please! I don’t have any knowledge about models, so I have no choice but to ask you to do my nails! Please help me!”
But when I saw the gal, who seemed invincible and carefree, desperately pleading with her hands together, I couldn’t help but want to help her—something I wouldn’t normally think.
“From my perspective, I think…”
“Yeah?”
“Nails and models being similar means there are only some common aspects. The tools, paints, and techniques are probably completely different between human nails and models.”
“Y-Yeah…”
It seemed that while Sayori Goto’s claws were different from those of normal humans, they still couldn’t be processed like a model.
Sayori Goto visibly drooped at that. The tip of her tail, which had been held high, drooped down, making it easy to see.
“So, I’ll study.”
“Eh?”
“I’ll look into how to do nails in my own way. I don’t think I can do it right away, but I’d like a little time—”
“Does that mean you’ll do my nails!? No way! I’m so happy!”
“Wait! I need to research first!”
I had zero knowledge! I had to figure things out from scratch. I didn’t even know if I could really apply modeler techniques.
“Yay! I finally have a nail artist!”
Sayori Goto jumped up and down, raising both hands.
“Stop! Listen to me! First, let me study!”
“Yeah, yeah, I get it! Just the fact that you’re willing to study makes me so happy!”
Sayori Goto had a beaming smile.
It seemed my enthusiasm had reached her.
“...I have no experience with nails. I really don’t know if I can do it.”
“I thought you’d say it was impossible! Just saying that is already a huge thank you!”
“Did you ask me as a last resort?”
“Isn’t it better to ask than to not say anything? If I get turned down, then that’s that.”
It seemed she thought if it didn’t work out, it couldn’t be helped. However, for an introvert, the option to decline didn’t really exist in the first place.

But I didn’t feel like I was just being swept along. I had developed a bit of interest in the nails Sayori Goto mentioned, and if I could use my knowledge to help her, that would make me a little happy too.
“I’m borrowing my dad’s garage.”
“Garage? A place to park a car?”

“Yeah. My dad works at a car repair shop, specializing in painting cars. This garage is a building my dad owns to balance work and hobbies. Sometimes, there are cars parked that he’s been asked to paint.”
What I borrowed from my dad was the office next to the garage. Since my dad hardly used this office, he let me use it for making models. Now, it had completely become my workspace.
“Phew.”
I sat down at the desk for making models and took a breath.
On the desk were all the tools needed for model-making: nippers, design knives, various drills and files, and more. There was also a work mat to protect the desk and a light to brighten my workspace.

Beside me was a painting booth, an airbrush, and a compressor, along with various paints and solvents. Additionally, there were measuring cups and stirring sticks for mixing paint, brushes, markers, and so on.
In the back of the office, I had a display case where I showcased my best models, posed with great care.
(…Yeah, they look cool today too.)
I took pride in the fact that they were better than the display examples at regular model shops.
Even though I was alone, I could immerse myself in a sense of fulfillment and achievement through model-making.
In the back space, I stored models I planned to make in the future and leftover junk parts from the process of making or modifying models.

Even though it was part of a garage, I had all the tools necessary for model-making, and it was well-ventilated, making painting perfect. My dad said he was just lending me a place he wasn’t using, but for a modeler, it was like heaven. I couldn’t be more grateful.
Normally, I would dive right into making models, but—
“Alright then.”
I laid out what I had purchased on the desk.
It was a collection of small bottles filled with colorful paint. Nail polish paint.
(For now, what I want to do is just paint this—)
When a guy hears “nail polish,” the first image that comes to mind is probably these small bottles.
When you twist the cap, you can directly paint your nails with the brush attached to the underside of the cap.
The official name is Nail Polish.
It’s the most convenient and straightforward form of nail polish.
(From what I’ve researched, it’s almost the same as painting models with a brush—)
I opened a random small bottle and lightly painted my own nails with the brush attached to the cap.
A beautiful pink paint coated my nails. The paint layer was even and had a decent thickness. The adhesion of the paint wasn’t bad either.
(…Why can’t I paint Sayori Goto’s nails?)
I didn’t understand the reason.
Moreover, Sayori Goto had been more focused on filing her nails than painting them. Did she use a metal file to shape them?
(No, probably it’s more like a base treatment before painting.)
To achieve an even and uniform paint job on a model, it’s necessary to form a “paint layer”—a layer created by the paint.
This layer needs to have a certain thickness to produce the desired color.
It was likely the same when painting with nail polish.
Sometimes, if the paint doesn’t adhere well, this “paint layer” can’t be formed properly.
In such cases, you would do a base treatment, like filing with sandpaper, to ensure the paint forms a good layer.
(For some reason—Sayori Goto’s nails can’t form a paint layer. So she tried to do a base treatment…?)
In any case, it seemed that the claws of the dragon girl, Sayori Goto, were different from those of ordinary humans.
As I gazed at my pink-glimmering index finger, I pondered for a moment. I had started to understand a bit about nails, but I needed to see Sayori Goto’s nails first—
“Ahh! Azuma-kun, you’re painting with polish!”
